children: Saloni Shukla Mumbai: HDFC Bank, India's second-largest by both deposits and assets, is bringing critical digital banking and payment platforms in-house after repeated cyberattacks on fintech companies, non-bank lenders, and vulnerable application programming interfaces (APIs) exposed third-party outsourcing risks in the financing industry. "We are bringing our card platforms, including MyCards and OnlyCards, in-house.

We are also in the process of insourcing PayZapp," Ramesh Lakshminarayanan, group head of information technology and chief information officer at the country's most-valued lender, told ET. "Several third-party applications are being brought in-house." HDFC Bank aims to eventually develop and maintain 70% of its key applications in-house, particularly mobile banking, net banking and payments platforms. The lender, which had previously faced regulatory curbs over technology gaps in some customer deliverables, has also shut down BizX, a third-party platform serving small proprietorships, and integrated its functionality into existing systems.

title: HDFC Bank to Bring Key Digital Apps In-house amid Rising Third-party Risks
